workflows.workflow: Finding information across distributed documentation systems
workflows.pain_point: Information is scattered across multiple platforms (GitHub, Confluence, Jira, internal documents) making it difficult to locate relevant information
workflows.current_process: Manual search across GitHub, Confluence, Jira, and internal documents
workflows.evidence: Michael: 'We also have information spread across GitHub, Confluence, Jira, and internal documents. Finding the right information is probably half the problem.'

workflows.workflow: Finding accurate technical documentation across multiple systems
workflows.pain_point: Documentation is outdated and doesn't match actual implementation in code, requiring developers to search multiple systems and ask colleagues
workflows.current_process: Search Confluence, GitHub, Jira, and Slack for information; if answer not found, ask team members who may be unavailable
workflows.evidence: Sneha: 'Usually we search Confluence, GitHub, Jira, and Slack. If we still can't find the answer, we ask someone on the team.' Daniel: 'And that's a problem because the person who knows the answer might be on another team or on leave.'

workflows.workflow: Identifying discrepancies between code and documentation
workflows.pain_point: Developers discover documentation-code mismatches only when trying to use the documentation, wasting time and creating confusion
workflows.current_process: No proactive process; discrepancies discovered reactively when developers attempt to use documentation
workflows.evidence: Daniel: 'A developer can look at a Confluence page and then discover that the actual implementation in GitHub is completely different.' Sneha: 'I'd be interested in something that could look at the code and existing documentation and identify where they don't match.'

workflows.workflow: Finding answers in internal documentation
workflows.pain_point: Documentation is spread across multiple platforms and doesn't always explain how everything fits together; finding specific answers takes much longer than asking an experienced engineer
workflows.current_process: Searching across Confluence, GitHub, and internal wikis; documentation exists but is fragmented
workflows.evidence: Sameer: 'There is documentation, but it's spread across Confluence, GitHub, and internal wikis. Some of it is useful, but it doesn't always explain how everything fits together.' Daniel: 'A new engineer might ask me, "How does the payments service communicate with the customer service?" I can explain it, but finding that answer in our documentation can take much longer.'

workflows.workflow: Keeping technical documentation synchronized with code changes
workflows.pain_point: Documentation becomes outdated when code changes, and manual synchronization efforts have not been effective
workflows.current_process: Manual documentation updates attempted but not working well; documentation often describes older versions of implementations
workflows.evidence: Maria: 'We have talked about improving our documentation process, but keeping everything synchronized manually hasn't worked very well.' Sneha: 'I'll follow documentation to understand a service and then realize the documentation describes an older version.'

workflows.workflow: Generating documentation for API changes and new services
workflows.pain_point: Documentation creation when developers change APIs or introduce new services is not happening consistently
workflows.evidence: Daniel: 'It could also help generate documentation when a developer changes an API or introduces a new service.' Maria: 'But I don't want automatically generated documentation going live without someone reviewing it.' Sneha: 'Agreed. The AI should propose changes, not publish them automatically.'

workflows.workflow: Setup documentation maintenance
workflows.pain_point: Setup documentation becomes outdated as dependencies change, reducing its effectiveness
workflows.current_process: Create and maintain setup documentation manually
workflows.evidence: Jonathan stated 'We've created setup documentation, but it gets outdated as dependencies change.'

workflows.workflow: Answering developer questions about AI policy compliance
workflows.pain_point: Security team receives many policy-related questions from developers about what they can and cannot input into AI tools
workflows.current_process: Developers ask Security team directly when they are unsure about AI policy interpretation
workflows.evidence: Faisal: 'We've received several questions about whether developers can use AI with production code, internal documentation, or data from customer systems.' and 'Fewer policy-related questions coming directly to Security'

workflows.workflow: Interpreting AI policy for engineering scenarios
workflows.pain_point: Engineering managers don't always know the approved answer when developers ask whether they can use AI with specific internal repositories
workflows.current_process: Developers interpret general AI policy differently, leading to inconsistent application across teams
workflows.evidence: Laura: 'I've had developers ask me whether they can use AI to analyze certain internal repositories. I don't always know what the approved answer is.' and Faisal: 'We have a general AI policy, but it doesn't cover every engineering scenario. Developers are interpreting it differently.'

workflows.workflow: Training developers on AI security controls
workflows.pain_point: Telling developers to follow policy isn't enough if they don't understand why the controls exist
workflows.current_process: Unclear - training appears to be needed but not currently implemented
workflows.evidence: Karen: 'I'd also like to see some form of training. Telling developers to follow a policy isn't enough if they don't understand why the controls exist.' and Laura: 'If we had clear examples, developers would probably be more comfortable using the tool.'

workflows.workflow: Code review of tests created by junior developers
workflows.pain_point: Senior engineers spend time reviewing tests created by junior developers rather than writing tests themselves
workflows.current_process: Senior engineers review test code written by junior developers
workflows.evidence: Mark: 'the senior engineers probably spend less time writing the tests themselves and more time reviewing what the junior developers create.'

workflows.workflow: Code review process for pull requests
workflows.pain_point: Senior developers spending significant time reviewing routine and straightforward pull requests, creating a bottleneck
workflows.current_process: All PRs go through GitHub where one or two senior developers review, leave comments, developer makes changes, then another review cycle occurs. Automated linting and static analysis tools are used but don't understand context of changes
workflows.frequency: High volume of smaller PRs mentioned
workflows.evidence: James: 'Code reviews are probably one of the bigger time sinks.' Rahul: 'Some PRs are easy, but we also get a lot of repetitive changes where I'm basically checking the same things over and over.' Ananya: 'The problem is that our senior developers are becoming a bottleneck.'

workflows.workflow: Understanding legacy code and service dependencies
workflows.pain_point: Engineers spend significant time (over an hour) understanding legacy code before making changes due to outdated documentation and information scattered across multiple systems
workflows.current_process: Search through repository, review old documentation, check Jira tickets, and ask colleagues who previously worked on the code
workflows.frequency: Several times per week across the team
workflows.evidence: Neha: 'When I get assigned an issue in one of the older Java services, I can spend an hour or more just figuring out what the code is doing before I can make a change.' and 'Almost every time someone works on one of the older services. Maybe several times a week across the team.'

workflows.workflow: Tracing service dependency chains
workflows.pain_point: Engineers must manually trace through multiple services to understand dependency relationships
workflows.current_process: Manual code tracing across multiple services
workflows.evidence: Michael: 'Even experienced engineers sometimes have to trace through several services before they understand the dependency chain.'

workflows.workflow: Engineering requirement refinement and ticket context analysis
workflows.pain_point: Engineers spend significant time manually reviewing Jira tickets, comments, related tickets, and Slack conversations to understand requirement context before they can estimate or start work
workflows.current_process: Engineers read through Jira tickets and comments, search for related tickets, review Slack conversations, and if unclear, schedule meetings with product managers for clarification
workflows.frequency: Every planning cycle, affecting a meaningful percentage of tickets
workflows.evidence: Vikram: 'Sometimes I'll spend 30 minutes just understanding the context of a ticket before I can estimate it.' Vikram: 'I'd love something that could look at the ticket, related Jira issues, and our existing documentation and summarize the context before I start working on it.' Vikram: 'If it saves even 15 or 20 minutes per ticket, that would add up quickly.'

workflows.workflow: Identification of incomplete or unclear requirements
workflows.pain_point: Product requirements often lack sufficient detail, causing delays when engineering discovers missing information during refinement rather than upfront
workflows.current_process: Engineers discover gaps during manual ticket review, then must initiate clarification cycles with product managers
workflows.evidence: Aisha: 'The problem is that this creates delays. Product thinks the requirement is ready, but engineering discovers missing information during refinement.' Robert: 'I'd also want it to identify missing information rather than just summarize what's already there.' Aisha: 'If the system could say, "The acceptance criteria don't specify what should happen in this scenario," that would be useful.'

workflows.workflow: New engineer onboarding and system context learning
workflows.pain_point: New engineers lack historical context about systems, making requirement understanding more difficult
workflows.current_process: New engineers must learn system history through ticket review and asking experienced team members
workflows.evidence: Robert: 'It's especially difficult for new engineers because they don't know the history behind some of these systems.'

workflows.workflow: Engineering onboarding and knowledge transfer
workflows.persona: New engineers and senior engineers providing support
workflows.pain_point: Getting new engineers productive takes longer than desired; experienced engineers spend significant time answering onboarding questions
workflows.current_process: New engineers learn by asking other engineers questions, reading documentation spread across Confluence, GitHub, and internal wikis, and watching recorded training sessions
workflows.frequency: Occurs regularly with each new hire; experienced engineers spend 2-4 hours per week during first month per new hire
workflows.evidence: Daniel: 'When I joined, I spent a lot of time asking other engineers questions. Even now, when someone new joins my team, I spend several hours helping them understand the codebase.' Daniel: 'Probably two to four hours a week during the first month for each new hire.' Emily: 'We hire engineers regularly, and getting them productive takes longer than we'd like.'

workflows.workflow: Developer environment setup for new developers
workflows.pain_point: New developers spend significant time installing dependencies, configuring services, getting credentials, and troubleshooting local environment issues
workflows.current_process: Developers follow setup documentation, manually install dependencies and configure services, troubleshoot errors by searching Slack, GitHub issues, and old documentation
workflows.frequency: Almost every time for new developers
workflows.evidence: Meera stated 'Someone might spend half a day installing dependencies, configuring services, getting credentials, and figuring out why something isn't working locally.' Omar confirmed 'For new developers, almost every time.'

workflows.workflow: Environment troubleshooting when switching between services
workflows.pain_point: Existing developers encounter environment setup issues multiple times per month when moving between services, requiring time to search for solutions across multiple sources
workflows.current_process: Search Slack, GitHub issues, and old documentation to find solutions that other developers used for similar issues
workflows.frequency: A few times a month per developer
workflows.evidence: Omar stated 'For existing developers, probably a few times a month when they move between services' and 'I usually search Slack, GitHub issues, and old documentation to figure out what someone else did.'

workflows.workflow: Writing unit and regression tests for payment services
workflows.pain_point: Developers spend significant manual time writing tests after completing features, particularly for older services
workflows.current_process: After finishing a feature, developers manually write unit and regression tests, which takes additional time beyond the feature development itself
workflows.frequency: Every sprint, sometimes more frequently for production bugs or larger releases
workflows.evidence: Alex: 'For some of the payments services, I'll finish a feature and then spend another couple of hours writing the unit and regression tests.' and 'Pretty much every sprint. Sometimes more if we're dealing with a production bug or a larger release.'

workflows.workflow: Updating and maintaining existing test suites when codebase changes
workflows.pain_point: When codebase changes, developers must determine which existing tests remain relevant and create new ones; much of this work is repetitive
workflows.current_process: Developers manually review existing tests for relevance after code changes and add new tests as needed
workflows.frequency: Ongoing as part of regular development cycles
workflows.evidence: Mark: 'When something changes in the codebase, we have to figure out which existing tests are still relevant and add new ones. A lot of that work is repetitive.'

workflows.workflow: Production incident investigation and context gathering
workflows.pain_point: Engineers spend 30-40 minutes manually gathering context from multiple systems (logs, dashboards, deployments, Jira tickets, previous incident reports) before they can begin actual troubleshooting
workflows.current_process: Manual investigation across multiple systems including logs, dashboards, recent deployments, Jira tickets, and previous incident reports to gather context before troubleshooting
workflows.frequency: Several incidents per week across services
workflows.evidence: Arjun stated 'An engineer might spend 30 or 40 minutes just gathering context before they start troubleshooting' and Kevin described 'We look through logs, dashboards, recent deployments, Jira tickets, and previous incident reports.' Kevin also confirmed 'We have several incidents every week across our services.'

workflows.workflow: Identifying relevant runbooks during incidents
workflows.pain_point: Runbooks exist but are not always followed because engineers don't always know which runbook applies to the incident
workflows.current_process: Engineers must manually determine which runbook is relevant to the current incident
workflows.evidence: Kevin stated 'We have runbooks, but they're not always followed because engineers don't always know which runbook applies to the incident.'

workflows.workflow: Finding similar historical incidents
workflows.pain_point: Engineers have years of incident history available but don't always know where to look to find similar past incidents
workflows.current_process: Manual search through historical incident records
workflows.frequency: During incident investigation (several times per week)
workflows.evidence: Kevin stated 'It would also be useful if it could identify similar incidents we've had before. We have years of incident history but engineers don't always know where to look.'

workflows.workflow: Understanding unfamiliar service architecture during incidents
workflows.pain_point: When an engineer investigates an incident for a service they haven't worked on before, they need to understand the architecture and recent changes before troubleshooting
workflows.current_process: Manual review of architecture documentation and change history
workflows.evidence: Lisa stated 'The bigger problem is when the person investigating hasn't seen the service before. They need to understand the architecture and then figure out what changed.'

workflows.workflow: Release notes preparation
workflows.pain_point: Manual gathering and reformatting of information from Jira tickets and GitHub pull requests into stakeholder-friendly release notes is time-consuming and inconsistent across teams
workflows.current_process: Developers and engineering managers manually review Jira tickets and GitHub pull requests each sprint, copy information from multiple tickets, and rewrite it into release notes that product and business teams can understand
workflows.frequency: Every sprint (smaller releases frequent, larger releases periodic)
workflows.evidence: Chris: 'Sometimes I end up copying information from five or six Jira tickets into a document and then rewriting it so it makes sense.' Tom: 'Release preparation takes more time than it should. The engineering teams have to gather information from Jira and GitHub and then prepare release notes for stakeholders.' Kavya: 'For a larger release, probably several hours across the team.'

workflows.workflow: Identifying relevant training materials
workflows.pain_point: Recorded training sessions exist but people don't always know which ones are relevant to their role
workflows.current_process: Recorded training sessions are available but discovery is unclear
workflows.evidence: Emily: 'We also have recorded training sessions, but people don't always know which ones are relevant to their role.'

workflows.workflow: Error message interpretation and troubleshooting
workflows.pain_point: Error messages aren't always helpful and developers struggle to determine if issues are with their machine, dependencies, or service configuration
workflows.current_process: Developers use general AI tools to explain error messages, but answers aren't specific to their internal environment
workflows.evidence: Omar stated 'when something breaks, the error messages aren't always helpful' and 'I've used general AI tools to explain error messages. That's useful, but the answers aren't always specific to our environment.' Meera noted 'developers often don't know whether the issue is with their machine, the dependency, or the service configuration.'
